lockup.summary: Directors, officers and certain holders cannot sell shares for 180 days after the offering closes without the lead underwriter's consent. The company also agrees not to issue new stock in that time.

what: It cuts, makes and installs stone countertops and surfaces for builders and homeowners in the Dallas-Fort Worth area.
proceeds: It plans to spend about $10,000,000 of the $17,750,000 net proceeds buying smaller stone fabricators, none of which it has yet identified. The rest goes to working capital, marketing, repaying a credit line and equipment.
risks: Demand for its work depends on the construction and remodeling industries, which rise and fall with the economy.
It competes with many stone fabricators, including small local shops that may charge less.
Lasting effects of COVID-19 or future health crises could disrupt construction, supply chains and its business.
It may struggle to hire and keep skilled workers, which could raise costs and delay projects.
Most of its revenue comes from the Dallas-Fort Worth area, so a local downturn or severe weather could hurt it badly.
